facts.text: The drift task is registered as Isaac-MushrDriftRL-v0 with entry point isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv and env_cfg_entry_point MushrDriftRLEnvCfg
MushrDriftRLEnvCfg extends ManagerBasedRLEnvCfg and sets seed 42, num_envs 1024 and env_spacing 0
The drift configuration sets sim.dt = 0.005 s (200 Hz) and decimation = 4 (50 Hz), so one environment step applies one action over four physics steps of 20 ms
The drift episode length is 5 simulated seconds
The MuSHR action group is an RCCarRWDActionCfg with scale (3.0, 0.488), base length 0.325, base width 0.2, wheel radius 0.05, no_reverse True and bounding strategy clip
The Ackermann action term reports action_dim 2: target velocity and target steering angle
apply_actions passes component 0 of the processed action as the target velocity and component 1 as the target steering angle
process_actions clips every action component to [-1.0, 1.0] before scaling, and with no_reverse set it clamps the velocity component to at least 0
The policy observation group concatenates root_pos_w, root_euler_xyz, base_lin_vel, base_ang_vel and last_action; last_action is clipped to (-1, 1) and the first four terms carry Gaussian noise
The project targets Isaac Lab 2.0.2 and Isaac Sim 4.5.0 on Linux 64-bit
Real-robot deployments are maintained in the separate RealLab repository, not in this clone
The upstream test starts Isaac Sim through AppLauncher and instantiates the task with gym.make(task_name, cfg=env_cfg)

determinism.notes: the fake fixes its initial yaw from reset(seed) and its kinematics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the upstream Isaac Sim task was not run and is not claimed to be repeatable

gaps: the fake backend is a kinematic single-environment stand-in: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, tire slip, actuator, sensor or noise model; the upstream Isaac Sim 4.5.0 / Isaac Lab 2.0.2 task was not run

the upstream task is vectorized (num_envs 1024 in the configuration and its test samples env.unwrapped.single_action_space); the fake models one environment with a 2-element action and a 14-element observation, so it is not the batched Isaac Lab interface
each environment step applies one action over decimation 4 physics steps of sim.dt 0.005 s, a 20 ms control period; timestep_ms names the 5 ms physics step, not the control period
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time only
the fake pays a constant 0.0 reward, never terminates and truncates at 250 control steps (5 s episode length); the upstream reward, termination and off-track conditions are not modelled
no physical device is modelled; real-robot deployments live in the separate RealLab repository
snapshot and restore are not offered: the fake exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
